newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba expects little change from U.S. after election.
newsitem.headline: Cuba expects little change from U.S. after election.

text.p: Cuba said on Thursday it expected little change in U.S. policy toward the island following President Bill Clinton's re-election, but expressed relief that the campaign "hysteria" was over.

"These elections don't mean a change in the composition of the political forces in the United States," Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Marianela Ferriol said. "We have no reason to expect any drastic change towards a sensible policy or respect for international law."
"At least we are relieved the hysteria of the election campaign has ended," she told a weekly news briefing when asked how Cuba viewed Tuesday's election result.
"The conclusion is that the status quo has been maintained," she added, noting that the Republicans would continue to control Congress.
The Clinton administration in March signed legislation tightening Washington's longstanding embargo against the communist-ruled island.

The Helms-Burton law aims among other things to discourage foreign investment in Cuba by punishing firms that "traffic" in property formerly owned by U.S. citizens and confiscated after Fidel Castro's 1959 revolution.
The law has been widely denounced by Washington's allies that do business in Cuba such as Mexico, Canada and the European Union, for its extraterritorial aspects.

Asked whether Clinton might now seek to ease U.S. policy toward Cuba and, in particular, the Helms-Burton law, Ferriol said: "We don't expect changes in this policy, although international rejection of Helms-Burton continues to grow".
Clinton, who had previously opposed aspects of the Republican-sponsored law, approved it after Cuba shot down two small private U.S. planes in February, killing the four crew.

Before the plane were downed there were signs of easing of tensions between the two countries and some Cuban officials had hoped that if Clinton were elected for a second term he might ease the 32-year-old economic embargo against Cuba.
